name: Pro Firm
summary: Calm, authoritative page for a professional practice: a large left-aligned headline beside an office photo with a floating 'Request a consultation' card, practice areas as tabs (accordion on phones), a numbered what-to-expect timeline, team cards, credentials and a disclaimer next to the FAQ, and an inverted contact band with hours.

sections.name: header
sections.what: Sticky glass header: monogram ({{initial}}) and name, page links on wide screens, a Call button always visible, a menu on phones
sections.edit: Keep the Call button. If you remove a section, also remove its link here and in the footer

sections.name: hero
sections.what: Eyebrow (name and city), two-part headline (strong first sentence, softer second sentence in .hero__soft), the tagline as a pull line, intro, call + 'How we can help' buttons, hours and office facts, the hero photo, and the consultation card (#consult) whose form builds an email or a text message
sections.edit: Rewrite the h1 around the owner's real promise; keep one h1 and the two-part shape. Keep the form fields short (name, phone or email, message). The form needs no server: app.js opens the visitor's own email or messages app

sections.name: practice
sections.what: Practice areas: each .area is an accordion item on phones; app.js turns them into tabs with a detail panel on wide screens (number, icon, title, description, 'Often a good fit when' ticks, 'Ask about this' link that pre-fills the form)
sections.edit: One .area per real service (3 to 6). Change the label in .area__label and the same words in .area__name and data-topic; keep data-no in step with the number. Delete extras; tabs rebuild themselves

sections.name: process
sections.what: About paragraph and photo, then a numbered 4-step 'what to expect' timeline (horizontal on wide screens, vertical on phones)
sections.edit: Write the about paragraph from the owner's facts. Keep 3 to 5 steps that describe how a new client is really handled

sections.name: team
sections.what: Three people cards with portrait photos, name, role and a short bio; a swipe strip on phones
sections.edit: Only real people with names the owner gave you; otherwise delete the whole section and its nav links

sections.name: faq
sections.what: Six questions in an accordion (details/summary), with the credentials card beside them
sections.edit: Answer with the owner's real policies (fees, appointments, privacy). Delete questions you cannot answer honestly

sections.name: credentials
sections.what: Nested inside faq: a card with a drawn seal (business name and city around the initial), a short list of registration / oversight / languages lines, and a disclaimer
sections.edit: Fill in only real registration or licence details the owner gave you and delete the other lines. Keep the disclaimer and adapt it to the profession (legal, medical, financial, property, insurance)

sections.name: contact
sections.what: Inverted band (ink background): headline, big phone link, email, consultation and Directions buttons, and a card with office address, opening hours (app.js splits {{hours}} into rows) and visiting notes
sections.edit: Replace the Visiting line with real parking or access notes, or delete that block

sections.name: footer
sections.what: Monogram, name and tagline, contact, hours, page links, copyright with a short 'not professional advice' line, back to top
sections.edit: Keep the links in step with the sections you kept

a quiet detail of the workplace: a desk, the reception, the treatment room or the building

behaviors: sticky glass header with an always-visible Call button
consultation form that opens a pre-written email or text (no server)
practice areas: accordion on phones, tabs with keyboard arrows on wide screens
opening hours split into tidy rows
Directions link built from the address
style_notes: Works best with: editorial-serif, clinical-clean, dark-luxury, swiss-grid, earthy-craft (newspaper and coastal also suit it). Tested under ten kit styles, light and dark, serif and loud, at 390 and 1280 px. Accent is only used as a fill (buttons, icons on accent tiles, rules), never as body text, so lime or orange accents stay readable. JSON-LD uses ProfessionalService; change @type to LegalService, Dentist, MedicalBusiness, AccountingService, RealEstateAgent or InsuranceAgency to match the business.
